title: ops-slate-consolidation-and-orchestrated-tasklets
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: consolidate scattered admin scripts and bite-sized runbooks into a single 'ops slate' of orchestrated tasklets that run on the Ops Runner. This ticket covers the conversion strategy, execution plan for the first tranche (top 20 support workflows), and the runtime/telemetry changes needed to operate runbooks-as-tasks with human-in-the-loop approvals, rollback tokens, and dry-run capability. We prioritize idempotency, clear audit trails, and measurable SLOs for time-to-remediate and success rate.
acceptance_criteria: Ops Runner supports a tasklet artifact format with typed inputs and checkpointing
Top 20 legacy admin workflows converted and validated in dry-run mode
Canary rollout mechanism routes 25% of live invocations to orchestrated tasklets with automatic fallback to legacy scripts on failure
Telemetry schema 'runbook_event_v2' implemented and dashboards updated to show time-to-complete, error-class, and human-approval latency
End-to-end tests and a migration playbook published in Confluence
Security review completed for KMS access and ephemeral credentials in Private deployments
tasks: Create tasklet schema and registry contract (inputs, outputs, checkpoint points)
Implement async worker pool in ops-runner with concurrency controls and priority lanes
Add Slack modal hooks + TTL approval tokens for human gates
Build rollback-token generator that is idempotent and reversible
Instrument runbook_event_v2 telemetry and add panels in Ops Console
Write migration script to dry-run existing bash/python admin scripts and emit conversion hints
Run conversion for first 20 workflows and run validation playbook
notes: Trade-offs considered: full rewrite vs automated transpile. We chose a hybrid approach—automated hinting + manual patching for sensitive workflows to reduce risk.
Risk: stateful scripts that mutate infra may require explicit checkpoint extraction; those will be fenced behind 'privileged' lanes and run on Dedicated capacity.
Design ask: Console needs a compact representation for multi-step approvals and an inline replay button for dry-run logs.
Performance: estimated 15-20% additional memory overhead for checkpoint snapshots; should be acceptable within Dedicated pool sizing assumptions.
Audit: all tasklet invocations will emit a cryptographically-signed provenance token persisted to audit log for on-prem retention requirements.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Banerjee: Kickoff: scoped first tranche (20 workflows) by mapping incident history and frequency. Prioritized tickets that are frequent, low-variance, and have clear rollback paths.

2026-02-18 - Marco Li: Implemented initial tasklet schema (v0.1). Schema supports typed inputs, optional checkpoints, and a dry-run flag. Pushed proto to repo for feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/1892

2026-02-22 - Priya Sharma (Product): PM review — asked for explicit success/failure semantics and a user story for support engineers. Suggested adding a 'why' field in the UI to capture operator intent for each manual approval.

2026-02-25 - Daniel O'Neil (Security): Security flagged KMS access for rollback-token signing in Private deployments. Decided: use ephemeral signing keys provisioned per-run with limited TTL; follow-up ticket to integrate with KMS provider.

2026-02-28 - Marco Li: Demoed dry-run conversion for 'refresh_kv_cache' workflow. Dry-run revealed an implicit dependency on a maintenance mutex — added explicit lock step to schema and updated conversion hints.

2026-03-03 - Design review (Nina Park): UX note — approval modals should show a concise diff of side effects (anticipated resources touched) and last successful run artifact. Action: Design to produce wireframes by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-05 - Marco Li: Completed telemetry scaffolding for runbook_event_v2 and created initial dashboard panels. Canary flag implemented; enabling staging canary next week. Open PR for worker-pool changes.
implementation_decisions: Adopt 'checkpoint-first' model: tasklets must declare checkpoint boundaries; runtime persists minimal state between steps to enable safe retries
Use hybrid conversion: automated transpiler emits tasklet skeletons + human verification for side-effectful steps
Run privilege-separated lanes: sensitive tasklets execute on Dedicated capacity with enforced RBAC
Approval flow implemented via Slack modal with signed TTL tokens stored as ephemeral keys in the audit log
open_risks: Missing idempotency in legacy scripts may cause unsafe conversions—we will block conversion until explicit compensating actions are added
Edge-case long-running tasks may exceed default TTLs for approval tokens; will add configurable TTL per tasklet
Telemetry cardinality increases; will add sampling for high-volume low-value events
qa_plan: Unit tests for tasklet schema validation and checkpoint replay
Integration tests exercising approval flow and rollback-token generation in staging
Chaos test: simulate worker preemption and ensure exactly-once semantics for idempotent tasklets
Runbook smoke tests: convert and dry-run 50 historical incident repros to validate behavior
migration_playbook: Step 0: Inventory scripts by frequency and risk (automated via 'ops-inventory' scanner)
Step 1: Automated transpile to tasklet skeletons and surface hints in Confluence
Step 2: Manual verification by owning engineer + dry-run in staging
Step 3: Canary 25% traffic with automatic fallback to legacy script on error
Step 4: Monitor metrics for two weeks, then scale up canary to 100% and decommission legacy artifact
